Subject: POC credit request — concurrent throughput check

Hi Soojin,

Quick note from OptiDocs — we're scheduled to run the final POC throughput/latency validation next Tuesday (9/15). The test run will simulate concurrent inference across 120 clients, peak ~500 RPS for short bursts, sustained ~120–150 RPS for 2–3 hours. Based on our rough estimates, we'll burn ~350k–450k tokens across the run.

Can Redwood provision a temporary credit buffer (trial credits / promotional credits) so we can run an end-to-end stress pass without risking throttles? Ideally: a one-time allocation usable for 72 hours that we can schedule around the test window. We're also happy to share the exact load plan and synthetic dataset.

Ask: approval for ~500k tokens (or equivalent credit) for a 72-hour window, and a short note on any rate-limit or per-account constraints we should be aware of.

Attached: brief POC plan (POC-load-plan.xlsx) — contains expected request profile.

Thanks,
Carlos Alvarez

OptiDocs, Inc.

Hi all — quick technical check from infra/solutions.

We can support the profile in the attachment with the following guidance:
- Warm-up: 15–30 minutes of progressive ramp to populate KV cache and ensure steady latency.
- Concurrency: we'll create a temporary quota bump for the account to allow the 500 RPS bursts. Please confirm exact RPS curve; I've added a suggested ramp schedule in the load script.
- Batching: set max_batch_size=8 and prefer request-level grouping on your client to reduce backend overhead.
- Memory: if you use rw-large-v1 fp16 you should be under current limits; quantized 8-bit will reduce cost and memory footprint.
- Telemetry: enable token-level tracing for the run (we'll redact PII) so we can analyze any tail latency spikes.

I'll attach a small helper script that our SREs use for simulated load: load-sim-script.sh. If you confirm start window I'll have infra pre-provision the temporary quota and schedule a short warm-up.

-Karthik
